figures.title: Comprehensive Taxonomy of LLM Security Threats Across the Model Lifecycle
figures.caption: Figure 1: A systematic categorization of LLM vulnerabilities divided into training-time threats, inference-time threats, and output-level flaws.
figures.description: A hierarchical tree diagram mapping the lifecycle phases to specific vulnerabilities. Training-Time branches into Data/Model Poisoning and Backdoors. Inference-Time branches into Prompt Injection, Jailbreaking, and Specialized Domain Attacks (e.g., Code LLMs). Output-Level branches into Intrinsic and Extrinsic Hallucinations.
figures.rationale: Establishes the foundational structure of the survey, providing readers with a clear mental model of how different attacks map to the AI lifecycle.

figures.title: Evolution of Data and Model Poisoning Attacks (2024–2026)
figures.caption: Figure 2: Chronological progression of backdoor and poisoning attacks, illustrating the rapid shift from text-based LLM exploits to multimodal VLMs and autonomous agents.
figures.description: A horizontal timeline plotting major attack frameworks discussed in Section 3, color-coded by the target modality (Text, Code, VLM, Agent, Infrastructure).
figures.rationale: Visually demonstrates the survey's core narrative regarding the rapid acceleration and increasing sophistication of attacks between 2024 and 2026.

figures.title: Minimum Poisoning Budgets Required for Successful Backdoor Injection
figures.caption: Figure 3: Comparison of the data poisoning budgets (as a percentage of the training dataset) required by recent state-of-the-art attacks to successfully compromise LLMs and VLMs.
figures.description: A logarithmic bar chart showing the extremely low data poisoning percentages required by various attacks, emphasizing how little malicious data is needed to bypass alignment.
figures.rationale: Quantifies the severity of the data poisoning threat by highlighting the shockingly low threshold of malicious data required to persist through safety fine-tuning.

figures.title: Reported Attack Success Rates (ASR) of Advanced LLM Exploits
figures.caption: Figure 4: Attack Success Rates (ASR) achieved by recent automated and infrastructure-level exploits against state-of-the-art AI systems.
figures.description: A standard bar chart comparing the ASR percentages of specific attacks mentioned in the text, demonstrating the high efficacy of modern jailbreaking and backdoor techniques.
figures.rationale: Provides hard quantitative evidence of the vulnerability of current systems, using the standard ASR metric defined in the Background section.

figures.title: The Trade-off Between Functional Correctness and Security in Code LLMs
figures.caption: Figure 5: Conceptual mapping of code generation paradigms based on their balance of functional correctness and security robustness.
figures.description: A scatter plot with 'Functional Correctness' on the X-axis and 'Security Robustness' on the Y-axis. It plots standard LLMs, poisoned RACG systems, and defense-augmented systems like CodeGuarder.
figures.rationale: Visually synthesizes the core argument of Section 5: that attackers exploit the model's bias toward functional correctness to silently introduce security vulnerabilities, and that new defenses must balance both.
